subject: Budget Preparation and Schedule Policy
overview: The School Committee approved a three-year Student Opportunity Act plan and passed a new budget preparation policy on first reading. The meeting also featured student recognitions and updates on major capital projects including the McGlynn Playground and the Medford High School building project.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved the consent agenda including bills, payroll, capital purchases, and minutes from multiple previous meetings.

items.title: Reports of Subcommittees
items.summary: Accepted reports from the Strategic and Capital Planning and the Curriculum, Instruction, Assessment and Accountability subcommittees regarding ongoing foundational planning.

items.title: Fine Arts Student Recognition
items.summary: Recognized students for their accomplishments in the Medford High School photo contest and the Scholastic Art Awards.

items.title: Announcement of New Leadership Positions
items.summary: Introduced Nancy Sherman-Hudson as the new principal of Missituk Elementary School and Christina Luongo-Dudley as the new director of Kids' Corner.

items.title: Bloomsack Leadership Awards
items.summary: Student recipient Oprah Nkera presented her research project on increasing representation and access to AP courses at Medford High School.

items.title: McGlynn Playground Update
items.summary: Reviewed construction progress on the city’s first universally accessible playground, which includes significant drainage remediation and new landscaping.

items.title: Student Opportunity Act Plan
items.summary: Approved the district's three-year plan focusing on early literacy screening and high school Saturday acceleration programs to address funding disparities.

items.title: MSBA and Building Committee Update
items.summary: Received updates on the high school eligibility phase deliverables, subcommittee planning for community engagement, and initial site evaluations.

items.title: Budget Preparation and Schedule Policy
items.summary: Approved on first reading a new policy establishing an eight-phase annual budget schedule designed to increase transparency and public participation.
